To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vaccine regimen used in the RV144 trial induces a broad and durable antibody response that includes antibodies to the V1V2 region of the envelope protein, antibodies to other regions of the envelope protein that bind to the envelope protein in a conformation dependent manner, antibodies with the potential to bind to the envelope glycoprotein in the native conformation, and antibodies that are able to neutralize a limited number of primary HIV-1 strains in vitro.
the vaccine regimen tested in RV144 induced HIV-specific antibodies and T cells, and these responses were correlated to protection against HIV infection.
the vaccine regimen tested in the Thailand trial induces a new type of immune response, which may play an important role in the modest protection observed in the trial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the correlates of immunity induced by the RV144 vaccine, and the design of new immunogens to elicit these protective immune responses.
understanding the role of the new responses in the vaccine-induced immune responses and their role in protection from acquisition of HIV infection.
the development of a new HIV vaccine that is safe, effective and affordable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RV144 trial is the first step in the right direction toward an HIV vaccine.
RV144 is a proof of concept that a vaccine for HIV can be protective in humans.
the vaccine regimen used in RV144 was able to induce immune responses that were able to reduce HIV acquisition by 31% (95% CI: 0.30-59.2%).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a new class of antibody responses to the V1V2 region of HIV gp120, induced by this new vaccine regimen in the Thai study, may be associated with protection from HIV acquisition.
we have been able to show that the vaccine induced antibody responses against the envelope protein of HIV and that this response was able to bind to HIV and neutralize the virus.

we have shown that the vaccine regimen used in Thailand induces a broad range of antibody specificities, including those that recognize the variable regions of the envelope protein, as well as the conserved regions, including the V1V2 loop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RV144 vaccine regimen induces a new set of antibodies that bind the V1V2 region of HIV gp120.
the vaccine induced antibodies that are able to bind to the envelope of HIV, but not the antibodies that are capable of blocking infection by HIV.
the RV144 vaccine regimen induced a strong antibody response against the HIV-1 envelope protein.
